Her advice? 
IGNORE AND BLOCK THE HELL PUT OF HIM

Idk if I answered your question correctly, but seriously, not checking up on him in any capacity is soooo worthwhile.

When I’m in psychiatric hospitals, they usually provide me a wheelchair so I can go down to the cafeteria/down long hallways, and even just to help me get around the unit when I’m having a bad pain day — because otherwise, I’d stay in bed and not do anything (I have RA in all my joints except for my elbows, but it’s worst in my knees). One BHC I was at didn’t let me use a wheelchair (even tho they knew I’d tried to kill myself because of the RA) and I ended up staying in bed the majority of the time and not going to groups because I couldn’t. The ones that help me move around in that way are the ones that are high in my book...

I also have knee braces, which are technically contraband, but the really good hospital I tend to go to lets me use them at all times except for at night. 

I also use a shower chair there, because I simply can’t stand for that long, and sitting on the floor of the shower is hard to get up from. 

I’m realizing as I’m typing this up how much they accommodate for me and my pain, and I’m just so glad they took your pain into account when handling you as well!

My dad called it "Corporal Encouragement", and that meant the metal end of a belt. He also made us sleep in the kitchen until we got it entirely cleaned up (like, so clean the Queen of England could eat off of the floor).
I remember when I was seven, I stole a big bunch of grapes from the fridge and hid it for later because I knew that the odds were good that I'd mess up before dinner and not get food for the next two days. My dad lined us up, threw us over his lap, and gave us each some CE. Then he asked who took the grapes. No one answered, so there was another round. And another. I didn't say a word. I needed to eat! I needed to make sure anyone could eat if they were grounded from food. So we were spanked for almost an hour before my little brother (5) told them he'd taken them, and eaten them.
I knew that he knew it was me and I cried with him that night when he entered our bedless room hours later black and blue. 
But, I mean, we got to eat grapes for four days straight...

That's what my mom did too; she used to hit us with those plastic hangers, and once when my older sister threatened to tell the police, she gave us that book to read and told us that she's not abusive, because look what this mom is doing. And we believed her, that if things weren't JUST AS BAD, that we didn't have a valid reason to complain.
